tools.description: Send an explicit diagnostic report to the uploads team (message + optional text log). Only call this when the user asked to submit feedback, a bug report, or error logs — never automatically. Do not include tokens, secrets, or private file contents. Same as `uploads report`.
tools.name: report

attachmentText.description: Optional text log/trace body the user consented to send (max 256 KiB). Not a file path.

command.description: Command that failed (e.g. put) — name only, no paths or args.

contact.description: Optional contact for follow-up (email or handle).

message.description: Short description of the problem (required, 5–4000 chars).

tools.description: Capture a URL or a local .html file and host it — a hosted, PR-embeddable image in one call. Backend `local` drives an already-installed Chrome/Chromium (dynamically loaded; unavailable in some runtimes); `remote` renders server-side via the workspace's render endpoint and counts against the monthly upload budget. Default via=auto prefers local when found, else remote. localhost/private-network URLs and .html files are local-only — via=remote (or auto falling back to remote) fails fast instead of a doomed request. Shares the put upload pipeline: optional frame, optimize-by-default, pr/issue attachment + comment, gallery, metadata. Uploads are public.
tools.name: screenshot

alt.description: Alt text for the markdown (default: derived filename).

app.description: Which surface is shown: web, ios, android, cli. Worth setting only when the same route exists on more than one surface.

browser.description: Explicit local browser executable path (local backend only).

cdp.description: Attach to a running Chrome via CDP instead of launching one (local backend only).

colorScheme.description: Emulate prefers-color-scheme: dark | light. Full media-query emulation requires via: "local" — the remote backend only sets the CSS color-scheme property and won't flip a page's own prefers-color-scheme queries.

comment.description: With pr/issue: create/update the managed attachments comment (best-effort).

destination.description: Typed destination root: screenshots | gh | f. With pr/issue must be gh or omitted.

dryRun.description: Capture + resolve key/URL without uploading. Not with comment or galleryId.

frame.description: Optional frame before optimize: phone | browser | iphone-16-pro.

galleryId.description: Add the uploaded object to this public gallery.

hide.description: CSS selectors to hide (display:none) before capture. Works on both backends.

keepExif.description: Keep EXIF/XMP/ICC when optimizing.

key.description: Explicit object key (default: <prefix>/<repo>/<ref>/<name>-<hash>.png). Cannot be combined with pr/issue.

metadata.description: Queryable custom metadata (key→value), separate from provenance. Omit to leave any metadata already stored for this key untouched; pass an object (even {}) to fully replace it. Keys: lowercase, ^[a-z][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$. Values: 1-512 printable ASCII characters. Caps: at most 24 keys, at most 8192 total key+value bytes. Canonical keys, which uploads.sh derives automatically where it can: url, path, env, theme, viewport, device, software, captured. Use `path` for the route (e.g. /settings) — that is the key `find_files` searches by, so spell it `path` and not route/page/screen. `gh.*` is reserved by convention for GitHub PR/issue attachment context (repo/kind/number/ref).

noGit.description: Don't derive the repo segment from git.

noHideDevTools.description: Don't auto-hide framework dev toolbars (Astro/Next/Nuxt/Vite), which are hidden by default for localhost/private-network targets.

noOptimize.description: Skip client-side image optimization (default: optimize to WebP).

optimizeMaxEdge.description: Max long edge in pixels when optimizing.

prefix.description: Key prefix (default: screenshots, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_PREFIX).

reducedMotion.description: Emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce so animations settle. Best-effort on via: "remote" (neutralizes animations via injected CSS).

ref.description: PR/issue/branch key segment (default: today, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_REF).

repo.description: owner/name repo segment (default: git remote, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_REPO).

selector.description: Capture one element instead of the viewport.

state.description: The UI state this image shows. Set it whenever the image is one side of a comparison — before/after is the most useful pair in a PR, and is what makes `find_files` with state=after work later.

target.description: http(s) URL, or a path to a local .html file.

wait.description: Settle strategy: load (default) | domcontentloaded | networkidle | a millisecond count (millisecond counts are local-only — via: "local").

width.description: Emit markdown instead of a plain embed.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

prefix.description: Key prefix filter, combinable with filters/name.

tools.description: Upload one or more files to uploads.sh and get public URL(s) plus GitHub-ready embed markdown. Backend `local` drives an already-installed Chrome/Chromium (dynamically loaded; unavailable in some runtimes); `remote` renders server-side via the workspace's render endpoint and counts against the monthly upload budget. Default via=auto prefers local when found, else remote. localhost/private-network URLs and .html files are local-only — via=remote (or auto falling back to remote) fails fast instead of a doomed request. Shares the put upload pipeline: optional frame, optimize-by-default, pr/issue attachment + comment, gallery, metadata. Uploads are public.

comment.description: With pr/issue: create/update the managed attachments comment (best-effort).

destination.description: Typed destination root: screenshots | gh | f. With pr/issue must be gh or omitted.

dryRun.description: Capture + resolve key/URL without uploading. Not with comment or galleryId.

frame.description: Optional frame before optimize: phone | browser | iphone-16-pro.

hide.description: CSS selectors to hide (display:none) before capture. Works on both backends.

maxHeight.description: Cap on full-page capture height in CSS px (default: 5000, 0 = uncapped). A page over the cap is clipped, with a `hint` in the result. Requires fullPage. Applied on both via: local and via: remote so behavior matches.

metadata.description: Queryable custom metadata (key→value), separate from provenance. Omit to leave any metadata already stored for this key untouched; pass an object (even {}) to fully replace it. contact.description: Optional contact for follow-up (email or handle).

message.description: Short description of the problem (required, 5–4000 chars).

tools.description: Capture a URL or a local .html file and host it — a hosted, PR-embeddable image in one call. Backend `local` drives an already-installed Chrome/Chromium (dynamically loaded; unavailable in some runtimes); `remote` renders server-side via the workspace's render endpoint and counts against the monthly upload budget. Default via=auto prefers local when found, else remote. localhost/private-network URLs and .html files are local-only — via=remote (or auto falling back to remote) fails fast instead of a doomed request. Shares the put upload pipeline: optional frame, optimize-by-default, pr/issue attachment + comment, gallery, metadata. Uploads are public.

alt.description: Alt text for the markdown (default: derived filename).

app.description: Which surface is shown: web, ios, android, cli. Worth setting only when the same route exists on more than one surface.

browser.description: Explicit local browser executable path (local backend only).

cdp.description: Attach to a running Chrome via CDP instead of launching one (local backend only).

colorScheme.description: Emulate prefers-color-scheme: dark | light. Full media-query emulation requires via: "local" — the remote backend only sets the CSS color-scheme property and won't flip a page's own prefers-color-scheme queries.

comment.description: With pr/issue (or auto-detected PR context): create/update the managed attachments comment (best-effort).

destination.description: Typed destination root: screenshots | gh | f. With pr/issue must be gh or omitted.

dryRun.description: Capture + resolve key/URL without uploading. Not with comment or galleryId.

frame.description: Optional frame before optimize: phone | browser | iphone-16-pro.

galleryId.description: Add the uploaded object to this public gallery.

hide.description: CSS selectors to hide (display:none) before capture. Works on both backends.

keepExif.description: Keep EXIF/XMP/ICC when optimizing.

key.description: Explicit object key (default: <prefix>/<repo>/<ref>/<name>-<hash>.png). Cannot be combined with pr/issue.

maxHeight.description: Cap on full-page capture height in CSS px (default: 5000, 0 = uncapped). A page over the cap is clipped, with a `hint` in the result. Requires fullPage. Applied on both via: local and via: remote so behavior matches.

metadata.description: Queryable custom metadata (key→value), separate from provenance. Omit to leave any metadata already stored for this key untouched; pass an object (even {}) to fully replace it. Keys: lowercase, ^[a-z][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$. Values: 1-512 printable ASCII characters. Caps: at most 24 keys, at most 8192 total key+value bytes. Canonical keys, which uploads.sh derives automatically where it can: url, path, env, theme, viewport, device, software, captured. Use `path` for the route (e.g. /settings) — that is the key `find_files` searches by, so spell it `path` and not route/page/screen. `gh.*` is reserved by convention for GitHub PR/issue attachment context (repo/kind/number/ref).

noGit.description: Don't derive the repo segment from git.

noHideDevTools.description: Don't auto-hide framework dev toolbars (Astro/Next/Nuxt/Vite), which are hidden by default for localhost/private-network targets.

noOptimize.description: Skip client-side image optimization (default: optimize to WebP).

noPr.description: Skip auto-PR context (issue #700): without pr/issue/key/ref/prefix/destination, a call on a branch mapping to exactly one open PR otherwise behaves as if pr had been passed. Also opts out via UPLOADS_NO_AUTO_PR=1.

optimizeMaxEdge.description: Max long edge in pixels when optimizing.

prefix.description: Key prefix (default: screenshots, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_PREFIX).

reducedMotion.description: Emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce so animations settle. Best-effort on via: "remote" (neutralizes animations via injected CSS).

ref.description: PR/issue/branch key segment (default: today, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_REF).

repo.description: owner/name repo segment (default: git remote, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_REPO).

selector.description: Capture one element instead of the viewport.

noPr.description: Skip auto-PR context (issue #700): without pr/issue/key/ref/prefix/destination, a call on a branch mapping to exactly one open PR otherwise behaves as if pr had been passed (stable key + managed comment sync when comment is set). Also opts out via UPLOADS_NO_AUTO_PR=1.

optimizeMaxEdge.description: Max long edge in pixels when optimizing (default: 2400).

prefix.description: Key prefix (default: screenshots, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_PREFIX). Cannot be combined with pr/issue.

ref.description: PR/issue/branch key segment (default: today, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_REF). Cannot be combined with pr/issue.

replace.description: Allow overwriting an existing object on a strict (non-gh/) key: explicit key, or the default put path. Default false — an existing object there is refused (key_exists) unless this is true or UPLOADS_OVERWRITE=1 is set in the server's environment. No effect on pr/issue keys, which always overwrite.

repo.description: owner/name repo segment (default: git remote, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_REPO).

state.description: The UI state this image shows. Set it whenever the image is one side of a comparison — before/after is the most useful pair in a PR, and is what makes `find_files` with state=after work later.

width.description: Emit markdown instead of a plain image embed.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Rebuild usage ledger bytes/objects from storage (source of truth). Preserves the monthly upload counter. Requires files:write. Same as `uploads reconcile`.
tools.name: reconcile

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Send an explicit diagnostic report to the uploads team (message + optional text log). Only call this when the user asked to submit feedback, a bug report, or error logs — never automatically. Do not include tokens, secrets, or private file contents. Same as `uploads report`.
tools.name: report

attachmentText.description: Optional text log/trace body the user consented to send (max 256 KiB). Not a file path.

command.description: Command that failed (e.g. put) — name only, no paths or args.

contact.description: Optional contact for follow-up (email or handle).

message.description: Short description of the problem (required, 5–4000 chars).

tools.description: Capture a URL or a local .html file and host it — a hosted, PR-embeddable image in one call. Backend `local` drives an already-installed Chrome/Chromium (dynamically loaded; unavailable in some runtimes); `remote` renders server-side via the workspace's render endpoint and counts against the monthly upload budget. Default via=auto prefers local when found, else remote. localhost/private-network URLs and .html files are local-only — via=remote (or auto falling back to remote) fails fast instead of a doomed request. Shares the put upload pipeline: optional frame, optimize-by-default, pr/issue attachment + comment, gallery, metadata. Uploads are public.
tools.name: screenshot

alt.description: Alt text for the markdown (default: derived filename).

app.description: Which surface is shown: web, ios, android, cli. Worth setting only when the same route exists on more than one surface.

browser.description: Explicit local browser executable path (local backend only).

cdp.description: Attach to a running Chrome via CDP instead of launching one (local backend only).

colorScheme.description: Emulate prefers-color-scheme: dark | light. Full media-query emulation requires via: "local" — the remote backend only sets the CSS color-scheme property and won't flip a page's own prefers-color-scheme queries.

comment.description: With pr/issue (or auto-detected PR context): create/update the managed attachments comment (best-effort).

destination.description: Typed destination root: screenshots | gh | f. With pr/issue must be gh or omitted.

dryRun.description: Capture + resolve key/URL without uploading. Not with comment or galleryId.

frame.description: Optional frame before optimize: phone | browser | iphone-16-pro.

galleryId.description: Add the uploaded object to this public gallery.

hide.description: CSS selectors to hide (display:none) before capture. Works on both backends.

keepExif.description: Keep EXIF/XMP/ICC when optimizing.

key.description: Explicit object key (default: <prefix>/<repo>/<ref>/<name>-<hash>.png). Cannot be combined with pr/issue.

maxHeight.description: Cap on full-page capture height in CSS px (default: 5000, 0 = uncapped). A page over the cap is clipped, with a `hint` in the result. Requires fullPage. Applied on both via: local and via: remote so behavior matches.

metadata.description: Queryable custom metadata (key→value), separate from provenance. Omit to leave any metadata already stored for this key untouched; pass an object (even {}) to fully replace it. Keys: lowercase, ^[a-z][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$. Values: 1-512 printable ASCII characters. Caps: at most 24 keys, at most 8192 total key+value bytes. Canonical keys, which uploads.sh derives automatically where it can: url, path, env, theme, viewport, device, software, captured. Use `path` for the route (e.g. /settings) — that is the key `find_files` searches by, so spell it `path` and not route/page/screen. `gh.*` is reserved by convention for GitHub PR/issue attachment context (repo/kind/number/ref).

reducedMotion.description: Emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce so animations settle. Best-effort on via: "remote" (neutralizes animations via injected CSS).

github.description: Scope via owner/repo#number or a GitHub issue/PR URL. Supplies repo when omitted. Mutually exclusive with pr and issue.

issue.description: Scope the feed to this issue. Mutually exclusive with pr and github.

path.description: Optional exact page-path metadata filter, for example /settings.

tools.description: Create a public newest-first screenshot feed (same product as CLI `uploads feed create`). Pass `repo` alone for the whole GitHub repo. issue.description: Scope the feed to this issue. Mutually exclusive with pr and github.

tools.description: Upload one or more files and get a public URL plus GitHub-ready markdown. Prefer `embedUrl` in GitHub markdown. Pass `contentUrl` for a public HTTPS file, or http://localhost on this machine, instead of a local path. With `pr`/`issue`, keys are stable and the managed comment is synced. All uploads are public. Accepts images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF), video (MP4, WebM, MOV), PDF, zip, gzip, and text (plain, markdown, CSV, JSON). SVG and XML are accepted only on storage lanes verified to serve them sandboxed (see the workspace's storage settings); HTML is rejected.
tools.name: put

alt.description: Alt text for the markdown (default: each file's name; with multiple files applies to all).

app.description: Which surface is shown: web, ios, android, cli. Worth setting only when the same route exists on more than one surface.

comment.description: With `pr`/`issue` (or an auto-detected PR): create or update the managed attachments comment. Best-effort.

contentBase64.description: Base64-encoded file content for in-memory uploads; requires filename.

contentType.description: Override the Content-Type (ignored when optimize rewrites the body).

destination.description: Typed destination root: screenshots | gh | f. Sets the key prefix; first-class alternative to prefix. With pr/issue must be gh or omitted.

dryRun.description: Resolve key + public URL without uploading (also previews a strict-key refusal via wouldRefuse). Not with comment.

file.description: Path of a single file to upload. Exactly one of file, files, contentBase64, or contentUrl is required.

filename.description: Filename for contentBase64/contentUrl (drives the key and content type). With single `file`, overrides the key's leaf (clean name) while keeping the pr/default path.

files.description: Paths of multiple files to upload in parallel. Returns { uploads, failures }. Cannot combine with file, contentBase64, contentUrl, key, or filename.

frame.description: Optional frame before optimize: phone | browser | iphone-16-pro.

keepExif.description: Keep EXIF/XMP/ICC when optimizing (default: strip for privacy on public embeds).

key.description: Override the object key. Single file only; cannot combine with `pr`/`issue`.

noGit.description: Don't derive the repo segment from git.

noOptimize.description: Skip client-side image optimization (default: optimize still images to WebP).

optimizeMaxEdge.description: Max long edge in pixels when optimizing (default: 2400).

prefix.description: Key prefix (default: screenshots, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_PREFIX). Cannot be combined with pr/issue.

ref.description: PR/issue/branch key segment (default: today, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_REF). Cannot be combined with pr/issue.

replace.description: Overwrite an existing object on a non-`gh/` key. Default false (or true if UPLOADS_OVERWRITE=1). No effect on `pr`/`issue` keys, which always overwrite.

repo.description: owner/name repo segment (default: git remote, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_REPO).

width.description: Emit markdown instead of a plain image embed.

attachmentText.description: Optional text log/trace body the user consented to send (max 256 KiB). Not a file path.

command.description: Command that failed (e.g. put) — name only, no paths or args.

message.description: Short description of the problem (required, 5–4000 chars).

app.description: Which surface is shown: web, ios, android, cli. Worth setting only when the same route exists on more than one surface.

browser.description: Explicit local browser executable path (local backend only).

cdp.description: Attach to a running Chrome via CDP instead of launching one (local backend only).

comment.description: With pr/issue (or auto-detected PR context): create/update the managed attachments comment (best-effort).

destination.description: Typed destination root: screenshots | gh | f. With pr/issue must be gh or omitted.

dryRun.description: Capture + resolve key/URL without uploading. Not with comment or galleryId.

frame.description: Optional frame before optimize: phone | browser | iphone-16-pro.

galleryId.description: Add the uploaded object to this public gallery.

hide.description: CSS selectors to hide (display:none) before capture. Works on both backends.

keepExif.description: Keep EXIF/XMP/ICC when optimizing.

key.description: Explicit object key (default: <prefix>/<repo>/<ref>/<name>-<hash>.png). Cannot be combined with pr/issue.

metadata.description: Queryable tags for later search (key→value). Use `path` for the route (e.g. /settings), not route/page/screen. Omit to leave existing tags; pass an object (even {}) to replace them. `state` and `app` have their own fields.

noGit.description: Don't derive the repo segment from git.

prefix.description: Key prefix (default: screenshots, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_PREFIX).

tools.description: Search the public uploads.sh documentation. comment.description: With pr/issue (or auto-detected PR context): create/update the managed attachments comment (best-effort).

destination.description: Typed destination root: screenshots | gh | f. With pr/issue must be gh or omitted.

frame.description: Optional frame before optimize: phone | browser | iphone-16-pro.

hide.description: CSS selectors to hide (display:none) before capture. Works on both backends.

contentType.description: Override the Content-Type (applied to every file; ignored when optimize rewrites).

files.description: Paths of the files to upload (at least one).

frame.description: Optional frame before optimize: phone | browser | iphone-16-pro.

fromBranch.description: Promote files staged under this branch name instead of the current branch (for a branch renamed before the PR opened).

keepExif.description: Keep EXIF/XMP/ICC when optimizing (default: strip for privacy on public embeds).

github.description: Scope via owner/repo#number or a GitHub issue/PR URL. Supplies repo when omitted. Mutually exclusive with pr and issue.

issue.description: Scope the feed to this issue. Mutually exclusive with pr and github.

path.description: Optional exact page-path metadata filter, for example /settings.

pr.description: Scope the feed to this pull request. Same product as a repo feed — one extra filter. Mutually exclusive with issue and github.

repo.description: GitHub owner/repo, for example acme/app. Required unless github is set.

tools.description: Get a workspace-owned change feed by ID, including its current newest-first screenshots and the canonical public /c/<id> URL. Anyone with the URL can view the media.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

cursor.description: Opaque continuation from a previous call's `cursor`. Pass it back unchanged with the same filters/name to get the next page; a null `cursor` means there are no more pages.

filters.description: Equality filters; all must match. Use `path` for the route (e.g. /settings), not route/page/screen. Optional when `name` is set.

name.description: Case-insensitive substring match on object keys (1–128 chars). Optional when `filters` is non-empty.

prefix.description: Key prefix filter, combinable with filters/name.

tools.description: Upload one or more files and get a public URL plus GitHub-ready markdown. Prefer `embedUrl` in GitHub markdown. dryRun.description: Capture + resolve key/URL without uploading. Not with comment or galleryId.

frame.description: Optional frame before optimize: phone | browser | iphone-16-pro.

galleryId.description: Add the uploaded object to this public gallery.

hide.description: CSS selectors to hide (display:none) before capture. Works on both backends.

keepExif.description: Keep EXIF/XMP/ICC when optimizing.

key.description: Explicit object key (default: <prefix>/<repo>/<ref>/<name>-<hash>.png). Cannot be combined with pr/issue.

maxHeight.description: Cap on full-page capture height in CSS px (default: 5000, 0 = uncapped). A page over the cap is clipped, with a `hint` in the result. Requires fullPage. Applied on both via: local and via: remote so behavior matches.

metadata.description: Queryable tags for later search (key→value). Use `path` for the route (e.g. /settings), not route/page/screen. Omit to leave existing tags; pass an object (even {}) to replace them. `state` and `app` have their own fields.

noGit.description: Don't derive the repo segment from git.

noHideDevTools.description: Don't auto-hide framework dev toolbars (Astro/Next/Nuxt/Vite), which are hidden by default for localhost/private-network targets.

noOptimize.description: Skip client-side image optimization (default: optimize to WebP).

noPr.description: Skip auto-PR context (issue #700): without pr/issue/key/ref/prefix/destination, a call on a branch mapping to exactly one open PR otherwise behaves as if pr had been passed. Also opts out via UPLOADS_NO_AUTO_PR=1.

optimizeMaxEdge.description: Max long edge in pixels when optimizing.

prefix.description: Key prefix (default: screenshots, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_PREFIX).

reducedMotion.description: Emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce so animations settle. Best-effort on via: "remote" (neutralizes animations via injected CSS).

ref.description: PR/issue/branch key segment (default: today, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_REF).

replace.description: Overwrite an existing object on a non-`gh/` key (e.g. an explicit `key`). Default false (or true if UPLOADS_OVERWRITE=1). No effect on `pr`/`issue`/branch keys, which always overwrite.

repo.description: owner/name repo segment (default: git remote, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_REPO).

selector.description: Capture one element instead of the viewport.

state.description: The UI state this image shows. Set it whenever the image is one side of a comparison — before/after is the most useful pair in a PR, and is what makes `find_files` with state=after work later.

target.description: http(s) URL, or a path to a local .html file.

wait.description: Settle strategy: load (default) | domcontentloaded | networkidle | a millisecond count (millisecond counts are local-only — via: "local").

width.description: Emit markdown instead of a plain embed.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Search the public uploads.sh documentation. Use this to answer questions about uploads.sh product workflows, including: attaching screenshots and video to GitHub PRs and issues; staging files before a PR exists; galleries; the GitHub App; comment config (.uploads.yml); hosted MCP and agent setup; screenshot capture and annotate; plans and limits; bring-your-own bucket. Same as `uploads docs`. Returns titles, URLs, and snippets. Pass `page` to fetch the full markdown of one page (slug, path, or URL). Omit `query` to list the catalog.

limit.description: How many search hits to return (default 5, max 50). Ignored when fetching one page.

page.description: Fetch one page as markdown. Accepts a slug (`attach`), path (`/docs/agents`), or https://uploads.sh URL.

query.description: Search query (e.g. 'stage before a PR'). A single slug like 'attach' fetches that page.

tools.description: Set or delete queryable tags on an existing file. `set` wins over `delete` for the same key. Requires `set` and/or `delete`. Same as `uploads meta set`.
tools.name: set_metadata

key.description: Object key to update.

set.description: Keys to set or overwrite. Use `path` for the route (e.g. /settings), not route/page/screen.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: List files staged for a git branch and whether they will auto-attach when a PR opens. Returns `{ repo, branch, files, binding }`.
tools.name: staged

branch.description: Branch name (default: current git branch, worktree-safe).

repo.description: owner/name repo (default: gh/git remote inference).

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Workspace storage and monthly upload counters (and remaining headroom when budgets are configured). Same as `uploads usage`.
tools.name: usage

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Show the active uploads.sh identity: workspace, API URL, and token scopes. Use this to learn which workspace you're talking to. A successful result also means the API is up. For a full setup diagnosis, use `doctor`.
tools.name: whoami

tools.description: Upload one or more files as stable PR/issue attachments (in parallel) and maintain a managed GitHub comment. Returns `uploads` and `failures` (one bad file does not abort the batch). Each success has `url`, `embedUrl`, and `markdown` (prefer embedUrl for GitHub). With no pr/issue, targets the current branch PR, and files already staged for that branch are promoted into it (`promotion`/`promoteError`; renamed branches are followed automatically, or name the old branch with fromBranch). Attachments are public and keys are predictable; upload only non-sensitive media.
tools.name: attach

app.description: Which surface is shown: web, ios, android, cli. Worth setting only when the same route exists on more than one surface.

contentType.description: Override the Content-Type (applied to every file; ignored when optimize rewrites).

files.description: Paths of the files to upload (at least one).

frame.description: Optional frame before optimize: phone | browser | iphone-16-pro.

fromBranch.description: Promote files staged under this branch name instead of the current branch (for a branch renamed before the PR opened).

keepExif.description: Keep EXIF/XMP/ICC when optimizing (default: strip for privacy on public embeds).

metadata.description: Queryable tags for later search (key→value). Use `path` for the route (e.g. /settings), not route/page/screen. Omit to leave existing tags; pass an object (even {}) to replace them. `state` and `app` have their own fields.

noComment.description: Upload only; don't create/update the managed comment.

noOptimize.description: Skip client-side image optimization (default: optimize still images to WebP).

noPromote.description: Skip promoting files staged for the current branch into the PR.

optimizeMaxEdge.description: Max long edge in pixels when optimizing (default: 2400).

state.description: The UI state this image shows. Set it whenever the image is one side of a comparison — before/after is the most useful pair in a PR, and is what makes `find_files` with state=after work later.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Read recent uploads.sh product updates (platform and CLI). Returns the latest entries with titles, dates, summaries, and a link to the full changelog at https://uploads.sh/changelog. Same as `uploads changelog`.
tools.name: changelog

limit.description: How many entries to return (default 5, max 50).

tools.description: Create or update the managed attachments comment on a GitHub PR or issue, listing everything uploaded for it. Posts as uploads-sh[bot] when the GitHub App is installed on the repo; otherwise via local gh auth. Edits its own prior comment in place and never touches other comments.
tools.name: comment

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Permanently delete one uploaded file by key, along with its metadata. Set dryRun to preview without deleting.
tools.name: delete

dryRun.description: Report what would be deleted without deleting.

key.description: Object key to delete.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Diagnose the configuration: API health, token auth, and workspace/token alignment. Returns the same report as `uploads doctor --json`, including hints.
tools.name: doctor

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Create a public newest-first screenshot feed (same product as CLI `uploads feed create`). Pass `repo` alone for the whole GitHub repo. Pass `pr` plus `repo` — or `github` as owner/repo#123 / a GitHub PR URL — to scope that same feed to one pull request. `issue` does the same for an issue. Optional `path` filters by page-path metadata. Creating the same scope again returns the existing URL. This is a live query, not a curated gallery. Anyone who knows the URL can view it. See https://uploads.sh/docs/feeds.
tools.name: feed_create

github.description: Scope via owner/repo#number or a GitHub issue/PR URL. Supplies repo when omitted. Mutually exclusive with pr and issue.

issue.description: Scope the feed to this issue. Mutually exclusive with pr and github.

path.description: Optional exact page-path metadata filter, for example /settings.

pr.description: Scope the feed to this pull request. Same product as a repo feed — one extra filter. Mutually exclusive with issue and github.

repo.description: GitHub owner/repo, for example acme/app. Required unless github is set.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Get a workspace-owned change feed by ID, including its current newest-first screenshots and the canonical public /c/<id> URL. Each item includes pageUrl (`/c/<id>/<item>`) for the pager. The feed may be repo-wide or scoped to one pull request / issue (see `number` and `kind` on the result). Anyone with the URL can view the media.
tools.name: feed_get

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Search files by metadata (`filters`) and/or filename substring (`name`). At least one is required. Same as `uploads find`.
tools.name: find_files

all.description: Follow the cursor and return every page, up to a bounded number of requests. A non-null `cursor` in the result means that bound was reached before the end — pass it back to continue.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation from a previous call's `cursor`. Pass it back unchanged with the same filters/name to get the next page; a null `cursor` means there are no more pages.

filters.description: Equality filters; all must match. Use `path` for the route (e.g. /settings), not route/page/screen. Optional when `name` is set.

name.description: Case-insensitive substring match on object keys (1–128 chars). Optional when `filters` is non-empty.

prefix.description: Key prefix filter, combinable with filters/name.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Add one existing, publicly served workspace object to a gallery. Reads the latest gallery version before writing, so the optimistic API version is handled safely. Does not upload or delete the object.
tools.name: gallery_add

objectKey.description: Existing public object key to add.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Create a public ordered media gallery in the workspace. The returned canonical URL is safe to give users, but anyone who knows it can view the gallery and its media.
tools.name: gallery_create

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Find workspace galleries linked to an external reference. Returns gallery summaries and canonical public URLs without contacting the provider.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Get a workspace-owned gallery, including ordered media and its canonical public URL. Gallery media is public to anyone with the URL.
tools.name: gallery_get

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Link a gallery to an external reference. References use provider-neutral fields; github currently accepts owner/repo#number or a strict GitHub issue/PR URL. No GitHub credentials or API calls are used.
tools.name: gallery_link

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Read the queryable tags on one file. Returns `{ metadata }` (empty when none). Same as `uploads meta get`.
tools.name: get_metadata

key.description: Object key to inspect.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: List uploaded objects in the workspace, filtered by key prefix or by a PR/issue's attachments. Paginate with cursor, or set all to fetch every page.

all.description: Follow cursors and return every page.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous call.

prefix.description: Key prefix filter (default: UPLOADS_DEFAULT_PREFIX + '/'). Cannot be combined with pr/issue.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: List metadata keys in the workspace (with counts). Pass `key` to list that key's values instead. Use before `find_files`. Same as `uploads meta keys`.
tools.name: list_metadata_keys

key.description: When set, return distinct values for this metadata key (with counts) instead of the key list.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Delete objects older than the workspace retentionDays setting, then reconcile. Skips if retention is unset. Requires files:delete. Same as `uploads purge-expired`.
tools.name: purge_expired

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Upload one or more files and get a public URL plus GitHub-ready markdown. Prefer `embedUrl` in GitHub markdown. Pass `contentUrl` for a public HTTPS file, or http://localhost on this machine, instead of a local path. With `pr`/`issue`, keys are stable and the managed comment is synced. All uploads are public. Accepts images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF), video (MP4, WebM, MOV), PDF, zip, gzip, and text (plain, markdown, CSV, JSON). SVG and XML are accepted only on storage lanes verified to serve them sandboxed (see the workspace's storage settings); HTML is rejected.

alt.description: Alt text for the markdown (default: each file's name; with multiple files applies to all).

app.description: Which surface is shown: web, ios, android, cli. Worth setting only when the same route exists on more than one surface.

comment.description: With `pr`/`issue` (or an auto-detected PR): create or update the managed attachments comment. Best-effort.

contentBase64.description: Base64-encoded file content for in-memory uploads; requires filename.

contentType.description: Override the Content-Type (ignored when optimize rewrites the body).

files.description: Paths of multiple files to upload in parallel. Returns { uploads, failures }. Cannot combine with file, contentBase64, contentUrl, key, or filename.

frame.description: Optional frame before optimize: phone | browser | iphone-16-pro.

tools.name: find_files

all.description: Follow the cursor and return every page, up to a bounded number of requests. A non-null `cursor` in the result means that bound was reached before the end — pass it back to continue.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation from a previous call's `cursor`. Pass it back unchanged with the same filters/name to get the next page; a null `cursor` means there are no more pages.

filters.description: Equality filters; all must match. Use `path` for the route (e.g. /settings), not route/page/screen. Optional when `name` is set.

name.description: Case-insensitive substring match on object keys (1–128 chars). Optional when `filters` is non-empty.

prefix.description: Key prefix filter, combinable with filters/name.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Add one existing, publicly served workspace object to a gallery. Reads the latest gallery version before writing, so the optimistic API version is handled safely. Does not upload or delete the object.
tools.name: gallery_add

objectKey.description: Existing public object key to add.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Create a public ordered media gallery in the workspace. The returned canonical URL is safe to give users, but anyone who knows it can view the gallery and its media.
tools.name: gallery_create

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Find workspace galleries linked to an external reference. Returns gallery summaries and canonical public URLs without contacting the provider.
tools.name: gallery_find_by_reference

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Get a workspace-owned gallery, including ordered media and its canonical public URL. Gallery media is public to anyone with the URL.
tools.name: gallery_get

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Link a gallery to an external reference. References use provider-neutral fields; github currently accepts owner/repo#number or a strict GitHub issue/PR URL. No GitHub credentials or API calls are used.
tools.name: gallery_link

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Read the queryable tags on one file. Returns `{ metadata }` (empty when none). Same as `uploads meta get`.
tools.name: get_metadata

key.description: Object key to inspect.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: List uploaded objects in the workspace, filtered by key prefix or by a PR/issue's attachments. Paginate with cursor, or set all to fetch every page.
tools.name: list

all.description: Follow cursors and return every page.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous call.

prefix.description: Key prefix filter (default: UPLOADS_DEFAULT_PREFIX + '/'). Cannot be combined with pr/issue.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: List metadata keys in the workspace (with counts). Pass `key` to list that key's values instead. Use before `find_files`. Same as `uploads meta keys`.
tools.name: list_metadata_keys

key.description: When set, return distinct values for this metadata key (with counts) instead of the key list.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Delete objects older than the workspace retentionDays setting, then reconcile. Skips if retention is unset. Requires files:delete. Same as `uploads purge-expired`.
tools.name: purge_expired

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Upload one or more files and get a public URL plus GitHub-ready markdown. Prefer `embedUrl` in GitHub markdown. Pass `contentUrl` for a public HTTPS file, or http://localhost on this machine, instead of a local path. With `pr`/`issue`, keys are stable and the managed comment is synced. All uploads are public. Accepts images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF), video (MP4, WebM, MOV), PDF, zip, gzip, and text (plain, markdown, CSV, JSON). SVG and XML are accepted only on storage lanes verified to serve them sandboxed (see the workspace's storage settings); HTML is rejected.
tools.name: put

alt.description: Alt text for the markdown (default: each file's name; with multiple files applies to all).

app.description: Which surface is shown: web, ios, android, cli. Worth setting only when the same route exists on more than one surface.

comment.description: With `pr`/`issue` (or an auto-detected PR): create or update the managed attachments comment. Best-effort.

contentBase64.description: Base64-encoded file content for in-memory uploads; requires filename.

contentType.description: Override the Content-Type (ignored when optimize rewrites the body).

contentUrl.description: URL to fetch and upload. Public HTTPS, or http://localhost / 127.0.0.1 / *.localhost on this machine. Filename is optional when the URL path has a leaf. Other private/internal hosts are rejected. Exactly one of file, files, contentBase64, or contentUrl.

destination.description: Typed destination root: screenshots | gh | f. Sets the key prefix; first-class alternative to prefix. With pr/issue must be gh or omitted.

dryRun.description: Resolve key + public URL without uploading (also previews a strict-key refusal via wouldRefuse). Not with comment.

file.description: Path of a single file to upload. Exactly one of file, files, contentBase64, or contentUrl is required.

filename.description: Filename for contentBase64/contentUrl (drives the key and content type). With single `file`, overrides the key's leaf (clean name) while keeping the pr/default path.

files.description: Paths of multiple files to upload in parallel. Returns { uploads, failures }. Cannot combine with file, contentBase64, contentUrl, key, or filename.

frame.description: Optional frame before optimize: phone | browser | iphone-16-pro.

keepExif.description: Keep EXIF/XMP/ICC when optimizing (default: strip for privacy on public embeds).

key.description: Override the object key. Single file only; cannot combine with `pr`/`issue`.

metadata.description: Queryable tags for later search (key→value). Use `path` for the route (e.g. /settings), not route/page/screen. Omit to leave existing tags; pass an object (even {}) to replace them. `state` and `app` have their own fields.

noGit.description: Don't derive the repo segment from git.

noOptimize.description: Skip client-side image optimization (default: optimize still images to WebP).

noPr.description: Skip auto-PR context (issue #700): without pr/issue/key/ref/prefix/destination, a call on a branch mapping to exactly one open PR otherwise behaves as if pr had been passed (stable key + managed comment sync when comment is set). Also opts out via UPLOADS_NO_AUTO_PR=1.

optimizeMaxEdge.description: Max long edge in pixels when optimizing (default: 2400).

prefix.description: Key prefix (default: screenshots, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_PREFIX). Cannot be combined with pr/issue.

ref.description: PR/issue/branch key segment (default: today, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_REF). Cannot be combined with pr/issue.

replace.description: Overwrite an existing object on a non-`gh/` key. Default false (or true if UPLOADS_OVERWRITE=1). No effect on `pr`/`issue` keys, which always overwrite.

repo.description: owner/name repo segment (default: git remote, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_REPO).

state.description: The UI state this image shows. Set it whenever the image is one side of a comparison — before/after is the most useful pair in a PR, and is what makes `find_files` with state=after work later.

width.description: Emit markdown instead of a plain image embed.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Rebuild usage ledger bytes/objects from storage (source of truth). Preserves the monthly upload counter. Requires files:write. Same as `uploads reconcile`.
tools.name: reconcile

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Send an explicit diagnostic report to the uploads team (message + optional text log). Only call this when the user asked to submit feedback, a bug report, or error logs — never automatically. Do not include tokens, secrets, or private file contents. Same as `uploads report`.
tools.name: report

attachmentText.description: Optional text log/trace body the user consented to send (max 256 KiB). Not a file path.

command.description: Command that failed (e.g. put) — name only, no paths or args.

contact.description: Optional contact for follow-up (email or handle).

message.description: Short description of the problem (required, 5–4000 chars).

tools.description: Capture a URL or local HTML file and host it. Shares put's attach, comment, and metadata options. `via=local` needs Chrome; `via=remote` renders server-side. localhost URLs are local-only.
tools.name: screenshot

alt.description: Alt text for the markdown (default: derived filename).

app.description: Which surface is shown: web, ios, android, cli. Worth setting only when the same route exists on more than one surface.

browser.description: Explicit local browser executable path (local backend only).

cdp.description: Attach to a running Chrome via CDP instead of launching one (local backend only).

colorScheme.description: Emulate prefers-color-scheme: dark | light. Full media-query emulation requires via: "local" — the remote backend only sets the CSS color-scheme property and won't flip a page's own prefers-color-scheme queries.

comment.description: With pr/issue (or auto-detected PR context): create/update the managed attachments comment (best-effort).

destination.description: Typed destination root: screenshots | gh | f. With pr/issue must be gh or omitted.

dryRun.description: Capture + resolve key/URL without uploading. Not with comment or galleryId.

frame.description: Optional frame before optimize: phone | browser | iphone-16-pro.

galleryId.description: Add the uploaded object to this public gallery.

hide.description: CSS selectors to hide (display:none) before capture. Works on both backends.

keepExif.description: Keep EXIF/XMP/ICC when optimizing.

key.description: Explicit object key (default: <prefix>/<repo>/<ref>/<name>-<hash>.png). Cannot be combined with pr/issue.

maxHeight.description: Cap on full-page capture height in CSS px (default: 5000, 0 = uncapped). A page over the cap is clipped, with a `hint` in the result. Requires fullPage. Applied on both via: local and via: remote so behavior matches.

metadata.description: Queryable tags for later search (key→value). Use `path` for the route (e.g. /settings), not route/page/screen. Omit to leave existing tags; pass an object (even {}) to replace them. `state` and `app` have their own fields.

noGit.description: Don't derive the repo segment from git.

noHideDevTools.description: Don't auto-hide framework dev toolbars (Astro/Next/Nuxt/Vite), which are hidden by default for localhost/private-network targets.

noOptimize.description: Skip client-side image optimization (default: optimize to WebP).

noPr.description: Skip auto-PR context (issue #700): without pr/issue/key/ref/prefix/destination, a call on a branch mapping to exactly one open PR otherwise behaves as if pr had been passed. Also opts out via UPLOADS_NO_AUTO_PR=1.

optimizeMaxEdge.description: Max long edge in pixels when optimizing.

prefix.description: Key prefix (default: screenshots, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_PREFIX).

reducedMotion.description: Emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce so animations settle. Best-effort on via: "remote" (neutralizes animations via injected CSS).

ref.description: PR/issue/branch key segment (default: today, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_REF).

replace.description: Overwrite an existing object on a non-`gh/` key (e.g. an explicit `key`). Default false (or true if UPLOADS_OVERWRITE=1). No effect on `pr`/`issue`/branch keys, which always overwrite.

repo.description: owner/name repo segment (default: git remote, or UPLOADS_DEFAULT_REPO).

selector.description: Capture one element instead of the viewport.

state.description: The UI state this image shows. Set it whenever the image is one side of a comparison — before/after is the most useful pair in a PR, and is what makes `find_files` with state=after work later.

target.description: http(s) URL, or a path to a local .html file.

wait.description: Settle strategy: load (default) | domcontentloaded | networkidle | a millisecond count (millisecond counts are local-only — via: "local").

width.description: Emit markdown instead of a plain embed.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Search the public uploads.sh documentation. Use this to answer questions about uploads.sh product workflows, including: attaching screenshots and video to GitHub PRs and issues; staging files before a PR exists; galleries; the GitHub App; comment config (.uploads.yml); hosted MCP and agent setup; screenshot capture and annotate; plans and limits; bring-your-own bucket. Same as `uploads docs`. Returns titles, URLs, and snippets. Pass `page` to fetch the full markdown of one page (slug, path, or URL). Omit `query` to list the catalog.
tools.name: search_docs

limit.description: How many search hits to return (default 5, max 50). Ignored when fetching one page.

page.description: Fetch one page as markdown. Accepts a slug (`attach`), path (`/docs/agents`), or https://uploads.sh URL.

query.description: Search query (e.g. 'stage before a PR'). A single slug like 'attach' fetches that page.

tools.description: Set or delete queryable tags on an existing file. `set` wins over `delete` for the same key. Requires `set` and/or `delete`. Same as `uploads meta set`.
tools.name: set_metadata

key.description: Object key to update.

set.description: Keys to set or overwrite. Use `path` for the route (e.g. /settings), not route/page/screen.

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: List files staged for a git branch and whether they will auto-attach when a PR opens. Returns `{ repo, branch, files, binding }`.
tools.name: staged

branch.description: Branch name (default: current git branch, worktree-safe).

repo.description: owner/name repo (default: gh/git remote inference).

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Workspace storage and monthly upload counters (and remaining headroom when budgets are configured). Same as `uploads usage`.
tools.name: usage

workspace.description: Override the workspace for this call (like the CLI's --workspace flag).

tools.description: Show the active uploads.sh identity: workspace, API URL, and token scopes. Use this to learn which workspace you're talking to. A successful result also means the API is up. For a full setup diagnosis, use `doctor`.

Row ordering, descending. tools.description: What the tokens from a period would have cost at another model’s list rates, alongside what they actually cost. Use this for "would Sonnet have been cheaper than Opus for this". It re-prices the exact token counts that were recorded, grouped by client, model and speed so the fast-mode premium and the two different reasoning-token conventions are handled correctly. Also reports what the same tokens would have cost with NO prompt caching at all, per model -- which is the figure that says whether caching is paying for itself. IMPORTANT: the model scenarios are a counterfactual, not a saving — the same task on a different model generally takes a different number of turns with a different context on each, and nothing on disk can say what that would have been. Report it as such, keep every scenario labelled an estimate, and never subtract a scenario from the reported cost to claim a number.
tools.name: counterfactual_cost

$call: Restrict to any of these clients. A single client id is also accepted.

Restrict which turns are included, by model id -- the same scope filter other tools spell `models`. Named apart here because `models` already meant "price against these" on this tool. Use both together to ask what your Opus turns would have cost on Sonnet.
Deprecated spelling of targetModels. Still honoured.

Models to price the selected tokens AGAINST. Not a filter on which turns are included -- that is `filterModels`. Omit to compare every model the pricing table knows. A model with no price is omitted and called out rather than guessed at.

tools.description: Token usage and cost bucketed on the time axis, newest first. Use this for "how much did I use yesterday", for a trend over a period, or -- with grain "hour-of-day" -- for "when during the day do I burn tokens". Buckets with NO activity are included and flagged `zeroFilled`, because omitting them hides the gaps and makes an ordinary bucket look like a spike beside one weeks earlier. All buckets are local time, so they agree with the period filter rather than drifting by a timezone offset. Cost is labelled reported vs estimated per bucket.
tools.name: daily_usage

$call: Restrict to any of these clients. A single client id is also accepted.
Look back this many days, counted from local midnight. Omit for all time.

Time bucket (default day). "hour" is a finer timeline; "hour-of-day" collapses every day onto one 24-slot local clock, which is what answers "when during the day do I burn tokens". All are local time, matching the period filter.

includeStatus.description: When true, also fetches /users/{id}/status and attaches the email/chat availability status under "status". Ignored when includeSystemActors is true.

includeSystemActors.description: When true, routes to the v3 /system-users/{id} endpoint, returning the system actor record instead of a standard user. Emits apiVersion: "v3". Takes precedence over includeStatus.

userId.description: User ID from listUsers, or "me" for the authenticated resource owner

tools.description: Get a Help Scout user or team report for a bounded time range. report selects /reports/user[/<report>]: overall, conversation-history, customers-helped, drilldown, happiness, ratings, replies, resolutions, chat.
tools.name: getUserReport

end.description: End of the reporting interval, ISO 8601

officeHours.description: Whether to take office hours into consideration (overall, conversation-history, chat)

start.description: Start of the reporting interval, ISO 8601

user.description: User ID or team ID for the report

tools.description: Get a Help Scout webhook by ID.
tools.name: getWebhook

tools.description: List all inboxes with IDs. Pass nameContains to filter by a case-insensitive name substring. Deprecated: inbox IDs now in server instructions. Only needed mid-session.
tools.name: listAllInboxes

nameContains.description: Case-insensitive substring filter applied to inbox names after all pages are fetched. Omit to list every inbox.

tools.description: List customer property definitions. Use to interpret custom property values embedded on customer records.
tools.name: listCustomerProperties

tools.description: List or search customers by name, query syntax, or dates. Defaults to v2 page-based pagination. Set useV3 (or pass a cursor) to use the v3 Customers API with cursor pagination, which also enables the email and createdSince filters.
tools.name: listCustomers

createdSince.description: ISO 8601 date - only customers created after this date. v3 path only (requires useV3 or cursor).

cursor.description: Cursor for v3 pagination (from nextCursor in a previous v3 response). Supplying this forces the v3 path.

email.description: Filter by email address. v3 path only (requires useV3 or cursor).

mailbox.description: Filter by inbox ID (v2 page path only)

modifiedSince.description: ISO 8601 date - only customers modified after this date

page.description: Page number for the default v2 page-based pagination (API returns 50 results per page)

query.description: Advanced query syntax, e.g. (email:"john@example.com")

useV3.description: Route to the v3 Customers endpoint (cursor-based pagination). Implied when a cursor is supplied.

tools.description: List Help Scout Docs article revisions.
tools.name: listDocsArticleRevisions

tools.description: List Help Scout Docs articles for a collection or category.
tools.name: listDocsArticles

categoryId.description: Docs category ID. Provide this or collectionId.

collectionId.description: Docs collection ID. Provide this or categoryId.

tools.description: List Help Scout Docs categories for a collection.
tools.name: listDocsCategories

tools.description: List Help Scout Docs collections, optionally scoped to a site.
tools.name: listDocsCollections

tools.description: List Help Scout Docs redirects for a site.
tools.name: listDocsRedirects

tools.description: List Help Scout Docs articles related to an article.
tools.name: listDocsRelatedArticles

tools.description: List Help Scout Docs sites using the Docs API v1.
tools.name: listDocsSites

tools.description: List organization property definitions. Use to interpret custom company property values embedded on organizations.
tools.name: listOrganizationProperties

tools.description: List all organizations with sorting options. Use for discovering organizations before drilling into members or conversations. Returns 50 per page.
tools.name: listOrganizations

tools.description: List saved replies for a Help Scout inbox. Use to discover saved reply IDs and inspect reusable response templates.
tools.name: listSavedReplies

inboxId.description: Inbox ID from listAllInboxes or server instructions

includeChatReplies.description: Include chat-only saved replies in the response

tools.description: List Help Scout tags used across inboxes. Use to discover tag IDs and exact names before filtering conversations or reports.
tools.name: listTags

name.description: Optional case-insensitive client-side tag name filter

tools.description: List Help Scout teams. Use to discover team IDs before team-member lookup or team-scoped reporting.
tools.name: listTeams

tools.description: List Help Scout users with optional exact email or inbox filter. Use to discover assignee IDs, mentions, and roles. Set includeStatuses to attach all user availability statuses; set includeSystemActors to list v3 system users (AI agents, integrations) instead.
tools.name: listUsers

email.description: Exact user email filter

inboxId.description: Inbox ID to find users with access to that inbox

includeStatuses.description: When true, additionally calls /users/status once and attaches all user email/chat availability statuses under "statuses" (not fanned out per user).

includeSystemActors.description: When true, routes to the v3 /system-users endpoint, returning system actors (AI agents, integration users) instead of standard users. Emits apiVersion: "v3". Ignores includeStatuses.

tools.description: List Help Scout webhooks. Use to inspect webhook configuration and discover webhook IDs.
tools.name: listWebhooks

tools.description: List Help Scout workflows. Use to inspect account workflow configuration and discover workflow IDs.
tools.name: listWorkflows

arguments.description: Arguments matching the selected operation schema. Omit for operations that take none.

tools.description: Search and list conversations. Filter by status, date range, inbox, or tags, and search content with contentTerms/subjectTerms, email/emailDomain, customerIds, assignedTo, folderId, or conversationNumber. Searches all statuses by default.
tools.name: searchConversations

assignedTo.description: Filter by assignee user ID (-1 for unassigned)

contentTerms.description: Match these terms in the message body (compiled to body:"term")

createdAfter.description: Filter conversations created after this timestamp (ISO8601)

createdBefore.description: Filter conversations created before this timestamp (ISO8601)

customerIds.description: Conversations belonging to these customer IDs (the customer->conversations bridge)

email.description: Match conversations involving this email (to/cc/bcc or customer)

emailDomain.description: Match conversations involving any email at this domain

fields.description: Specific fields to return (for partial responses)

inboxId.description: Inbox (mailbox) ID from server instructions

modifiedSince.description: Filter conversations modified after this timestamp (ISO8601)

query.description: Raw HelpScout query syntax (power users). The convenience filters below are compiled into this automatically. Example: (body:"keyword")

sort.description: Sort field

status.description: Filter by status. Omit to search active+pending+closed (excludes spam).

subjectTerms.description: Match these terms in the subject (compiled to subject:"term")

tag.description: Filter by tag name (comma-separated for multiple)

tools.description: Search customers by email address using the v3 API. Provides email as a dedicated filter parameter (vs query syntax in v2) and cursor-based pagination.
tools.name: searchCustomersByEmail

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination (from nextCursor in previous response)

email.description: Email address to search for

query.description: Advanced query syntax

tools.description: Search Help Scout Docs articles by query, site, collection, status, or visibility.
tools.name: searchDocsArticles

query.description: Search query

tools.description: Search ${$opaque} by user intent (conversations, customers, organizations, inboxes, users, reports, Docs articles, attachments). Returns matching operation names and descriptions. Start here, then load schemas with describe_help_scout.
tools.name: search_help_scout

query.description: What Help Scout information or operation is needed.

tools.description: Execute one enabled Help Scout write operation using arguments that match the schema loaded with describe_help_scout. Every operation changes Help Scout state. Operations whose mutation class is externallyVisible can email a customer, and each call to one is rejected before any Help Scout request unless it carries all three of: "confirm": true, "confirmOperation" set to the exact operation name, and "targetId" equal to the conversation ID in "arguments". Missing, false, or mismatched confirmation is refused. Operations classed nonDestructive or reversible need no confirmation. Set "dryRun": true to validate arguments and see the request that would be sent without contacting Help Scout.
tools.name: write_help_scout

arguments.description: Arguments matching the selected operation schema.

confirm.description: Must be true for externallyVisible operations. Ignored otherwise.

confirmOperation.description: Must repeat the operation name exactly, for externallyVisible operations.

dryRun.description: Validate arguments and report the request that would be sent, without contacting Help Scout.

name.description: Exact Help Scout write operation name.

targetId.description: Must match the conversation ID in "arguments", for externallyVisible operations.

tools.description: Cancel a rental. For verifications (ver_xxx) the API may refund if no message arrived. For long-term rentals (ren_xxx) cancellation is typically non-refundable - check the response.
tools.name: cancel_rental

tools.description: Create a new geo-targeted proxy list on a shared proxy. Provide either a single country (with optional region/city/isp/zip subfilters) or a countries array (2-30, mutually exclusive with the subfilters). To edit an existing list, delete it and create a new one.
tools.name: create_proxy_list

$call: Only valid with a single country.
2-30 ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 codes. Mutually exclusive with country/subfilters.
ISO-3166-1 alpha-2, lowercased. Mutually exclusive with countries.
Output format for entries[] (e.g. login_pass_host_port, http_url, socks5_url)
Only valid with a single country.
Only valid with a single country.
Only valid with a single country.

tools.description: Delete a proxy list. The list's credentials stop working immediately.
tools.name: delete_proxy_list

tools.description: Get the authenticated account: id, USD wallet balance, and per-endpoint-group rate limits. Use this before money-touching tool calls to confirm sufficient funds.
tools.name: get_account

tools.description: Read a dedicated number's status and received SMS messages (parsed codes included). Messages keep arriving for the life of the number; poll this tool after directing an SMS at it.
tools.name: get_dedicated_number

tools.description: Fetch the activation QR code for an eSIM as an image. Most MCP clients render the image inline so the user can scan it directly.
tools.name: get_esim_qr

tools.description: Read an eSIM's current status, plan info, and data usage. Combines GET /v1/esims/:id + /usage in one parallel call.
tools.name: get_esim_status

tools.description: Cascading geo discovery for proxy list targeting. No params -> countries; country=US -> regions; country=US&region=California -> cities; +city=Los%20Angeles -> ISPs.
tools.name: get_geo

tools.description: Read a proxy's status, usage, and gateway credentials in one call.
tools.name: get_proxy_status

tools.description: Read a rental's current status and any messages received. Pass the ID you got from rent_number (ver_xxx for verifications, ren_xxx for long-term rentals). SMS codes typically arrive 10-60s after rent_number; poll this tool until status changes.
tools.name: get_rental

tools.description: List the user's active and past orders across SMS rentals, dedicated numbers, eSIMs, and proxies. Note: ephemeral verifications (20-min single-SMS) are NOT listable - the rental id you got from rent_number is your handle to them.
tools.name: list_orders

tools.description: List proxy lists for a shared proxy (geo-targeted sub-pools that share the proxy's bandwidth).
tools.name: list_proxy_lists

tools.description: Buy a dedicated monthly number in a country from search_dedicated_countries. Quote-then-commit: the tool fetches your live price and ties max_price_cents to it so you never pay above the quote. Returns a ded_xxx id - poll get_dedicated_number to read incoming SMS.
tools.name: purchase_dedicated_number

$call: Auto-charge at the end of each monthly period
Country code or name from search_dedicated_countries (e.g. 'us', 'uk', 'germany')

tools.description: Purchase an eSIM plan. Quote-then-commit: the tool fetches the live price and ties max_price_cents to it so you never pay above what you saw.
tools.name: purchase_esim

tools.description: Purchase a proxy plan. Returns 202 Accepted with status=provisioning; the gateway becomes active in 1-2 minutes. Poll get_proxy_status until status='active'.
tools.name: purchase_proxy

tools.description: Re-rent the same number for another period at the current price. Only works on an expired rental whose re_rent_available is true (the provider has not yet released the number). Re-uses the rental's original duration; no duration argument.
tools.name: re_rent_rental

$call: ren_xxx from an expired LTR with re_rent_available=true

tools.description: Rotate the main proxy gateway password. Returns the new credentials.
tools.name: regenerate_proxy_password

tools.description: Extend a proxy's expiry by purchasing another period. Quote-then-commit.
tools.name: renew_proxy

tools.description: Rent a US non-VoIP phone number. kind='verification' (single SMS, 20min); kind='rental' (timed LTR with duration). For a private all-services monthly number, use purchase_dedicated_number instead. Quote-then-commit: the tool fetches the live price and ties max_price_cents to the quote so you never pay above what you saw.
tools.name: rent_number

tools.description: Reuse a completed/expired verification to receive another SMS. Free reuse is available when allow_reuse is true on the verification. Paid reuse ($0.50) is available when allow_paid_reuse is true.
tools.name: reuse_number

tools.description: Rotate a dedicated proxy to a new IP. Shared proxies rotate per-request through their lists - use create_proxy_list / list_proxy_lists instead.
tools.name: rotate_proxy_ip

tools.description: Rolled-up Redis health lint pass -- one call returns four categories of findings, each with a severity and an actionable fix: - big_keys: sampled keys whose memory footprint or element count is large enough to make operations O(N) and risk blocking the event loop on delete/expire. - missing_ttls: share of sampled keys with no expiry -- the classic 'cache fills up and OOMs' setup. - eviction_pressure: used/maxmemory ratio, active evictions, and the dangerous `noeviction` + no-TTL combination that turns a full instance into failed writes. - fork_latency_risk: long last-fork time, large dataset + active persistence, and failed background saves -- the causes of periodic latency spikes and durability gaps. Keys are sampled via SCAN (never KEYS), so it is safe on a large production instance; the big-key / missing-TTL findings are over the SAMPLE, not the whole keyspace.
tools.name: redis_advisor

$call: Flag a key at or above this many bytes (default 1 MiB = 1048576).
Flag a collection with at least this many elements (default 5000).
Warn when the last fork took at least this many microseconds (default 100000 = 100ms).
Treat the dataset as large (fork-risk) at or above this many bytes (default 1 GiB = 1073741824).
Flag when this fraction of the sample lacks a TTL (default 0.5 = 50%).
How many keys to SCAN-sample for big-key / missing-TTL checks (default 200, 0 to skip key sampling).
Warn when used/maxmemory reaches this ratio (default 0.8 = 80%).

tools.description: Run a single Redis command through the safety gate. Read-only commands (GET, HGETALL, LRANGE, TYPE, TTL, INFO, ...) always run. Mutating commands (SET, DEL, EXPIRE, HSET, ...) require ALLOW_WRITES=1. KEYS is blocked (use redis_scan). Arbitrary-execution commands (EVAL, FUNCTION, SCRIPT, MULTI, MONITOR, SHUTDOWN, CLUSTER, ...) are never exposed, even with ALLOW_WRITES=1 -- the gate is a curated allowlist, not a blanket 'anything when writes are on'. Use this for commands without a dedicated tool; prefer the typed tools (redis_get, redis_scan, redis_key_info) where they exist.
tools.name: redis_command

$call: Command arguments in order. For multi-word commands, the subcommand is the first arg.
Command must be a single alphabetic verb (e.g. GET, HGETALL); pass subcommands as args.

tools.description: Read a key's value, dispatching by type so you get the right shape without knowing the type in advance: string -> the string; hash -> field/value object; list -> array (LRANGE windowed by `limit`); set -> member array; zset -> [member, score] pairs (ZRANGE WITHSCORES, windowed); stream -> recent entries (XREVRANGE, windowed). Collection reads are capped at `limit` (default REDIS_MAX_KEYS) so a million-element list can't blow out context. Always read-only.

tools.description: Create many database records of one type in a single call and a single file write — the batch sibling of create_actor/create_item/create_weapon/create_armor/create_skill/create_enemy/create_state/create_class. Each entry in `records` takes the same fields its single create_* tool accepts (only `name` is required for most; omitted fields use the editor's defaults). Ids are allocated sequentially from the current max, so a record can reference a sibling created earlier in the same batch. Use this instead of N sequential create_* calls when authoring a cast, a loot table, or a skill list. Returns `{ type, count, created, warnings? }` (classes are summarized like create_class; enemy battlerName misses are warnings, never blocked). Throws — writing nothing at all — if any record references a database id that does not exist, naming the offending records[i].
tools.name: batch_create

$call: The records to create, each shaped like the matching create_* tool's arguments (e.g. for type "actor": { name, classId?, ... })
Which database the records are appended to

Reads the map's tileset flags. Returns per-direction passability (down/left/right/up — true = a character can walk off the cell that way), the cell's terrain tag, the stacked tile ids, and — when `direction` is given — a single `passable` boolean for that direction. Read-only.

$call: Optional: also report a single passable boolean for this direction

tools.description: Create a new actor in data/Actors.json. Only `name` is required; omitted fields use the editor's new-actor defaults (class 1, level 1-99, five empty equip slots, no traits). Allocates and returns the next unused actor id. NOTE: an actor's physical accuracy comes from its class + own traits — a class/actor with no Hit Rate trait (xparam id 0: trait { code: 22, dataId: 0, value: 0.95 }) always misses physical actions. The built-in class 1 has one; a custom class needs it added.
tools.name: create_actor

tools.description: Create a new armor in data/Armors.json. Only `name` is required; omitted fields use the editor's new-armor defaults (Shield equip slot, no stat bonuses). `params` is a flat 8-length stat bonus; `etypeId` is the equip slot (System.json equipTypes: 2 Shield, 3 Head, 4 Body, 5 Accessory). Allocates and returns the next unused armor id.
tools.name: create_armor

$call: Equip slot (equipTypes: 2 Shield, 3 Head, 4 Body, 5 Accessory)
8 flat stat bonuses [maxHP, maxMP, atk, def, mat, mdf, agi, luk]

tools.name: create_buff_skill

$call: Number of turns the buff lasts

tools.description: Create a complete, placed treasure chest on a map in one call — the two-page self-switch idiom done correctly, so the chest can never be looted twice. Page 1 (closed) is an action-button, priority-`same` event that optionally shows `text`, gives the contents, then flips its self switch; page 2 (opened) is gated on that self switch, shows the opened graphic and does nothing. `kind` picks the payout: item/weapon/armor (needs `id`) or gold. On the RTP `!Chest` sheet the open/closed states are the *direction* rows of one character block (down = closed, up = open), which is what closedDirection/openedDirection default to.
