tools.description: Cancel a running AI video generation job. Returns: {render_id, state}
tools.name: ai_gen_cancel

tools.description: Generate a video using a cloud AI model via fal.ai. model: kling-3.0 (best value), minimax-hailuo-2.3 (cheapest), luma-ray3 (best i2v), veo-3.1 (best quality), pika-2.2. image_path: optional reference image for image-to-video models. aspect_ratio: '16:9', '9:16', '1:1', '4:3'. Returns: {render_id, output_path, estimated_cost_usd} — background job.
tools.name: ai_gen_fal

tools.description: List all available AI video generation models with pricing and capabilities. Returns: {models: [...]}
tools.name: ai_gen_list_models

tools.description: Check the status of an AI video generation job. Returns: {render_id, state, progress, output_path, error}
tools.name: ai_gen_status

tools.description: Generate a video using local Wan2GP (FREE, runs on your 4090). prompt: describe the video you want to generate. duration_frames: number of frames (81=~3s, 121=~5s at 24fps). resolution: '832*480' (fast) or '1280*720' (HD) or '480*832' (vertical). steps: 8 = fast draft, 20 = quality. nsfw_mode: True = adds NSFW LoRA (wan_general_nsfw_v3 at 1.75). image_path: optional input image for image-to-video generation. Returns: {render_id, output_path} — background job.
tools.name: ai_gen_wan2gp

tools.description: Add background music to a video, mixing with existing audio. music_volume: 0.1=very quiet background, 0.25=subtle, 0.5=equal mix. duck_under_voice: reduce music when original audio is loud (sidechain ducking). fade_out_s: music fade-out duration at end. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: aud_add_music

tools.description: Extract audio track from a video file. format: 'wav', 'mp3', 'aac', 'flac'. Returns: {output_path, duration_s}
tools.name: aud_extract

tools.description: Mix multiple audio/video files' audio tracks together. input_paths: up to 8 files to mix. volumes: per-track volume multipliers (1.0 = unity). Defaults to equal mix. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: aud_mix

tools.description: Normalize audio to a target loudness (EBU R128 two-pass). target_lufs: -16.0 = YouTube/streaming, -23.0 = broadcast/EBU R128, -14.0 = Spotify. Returns: {output_path, target_lufs}
tools.name: aud_normalize

tools.description: Replace the audio track of a video with a new audio file. mix_original: 0.0 = completely replace, 0.3 = 30% original + 70% new audio. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: aud_replace

tools.description: Remove audio from a video (mute / silent output). Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: aud_silence

tools.description: Create a named video project to track multiple clips and settings. name: project name (used as identifier). clips: optional list of initial clip paths to add. Returns: {project_id, name, clip_count}
tools.name: proj_create

tools.description: List all projects, or get details for a specific project. project_id: if empty, lists all projects. If set, returns that project's clips. Returns: {projects: [...]} or {project: {..., clips: [...]}}
tools.name: proj_list

tools.description: Render all clips in a project as a single final video. Clips are concatenated in order with optional transitions between them. transition: 'none', 'fade', 'dissolve', 'wipeleft', 'wiperight'. music_path: optional background music track to add. Returns: {render_id, output_path} — runs as background job.
tools.name: proj_render

tools.description: Cancel a running background render job. render_id: the render_id of the job to cancel. Returns: {render_id, state}
tools.name: render_cancel

tools.description: List all render jobs (running, completed, failed). Returns: {jobs: [...], counts: {running, done, failed, cancelled}}
tools.name: render_list

tools.description: Check the status of any background render job. render_id: the render_id returned when a background job was started. Returns: {render_id, state, progress, output_path, error, description} States: pending, running, done, failed, cancelled
tools.name: render_status

tools.description: Embed chapter markers into a video file. chapters: list of {title: str, start_s: float} dicts. Example: [{"title": "Intro", "start_s": 0}, {"title": "Demo", "start_s": 30}] Returns: {output_path, chapter_count}
tools.name: vid_chapters

tools.description: Remove green/blue screen and composite over a background. foreground_path: footage with green/blue screen. background_path: background video or image. key_color: 'green', 'blue', or hex like '0x3CB043'. similarity: 0.1 = tight key (needs clean lighting), 0.3 = loose key. blend: 0.0 = hard edge, 0.15 = soft anti-aliased edge. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_chromakey

tools.description: Concatenate multiple video clips in order. input_paths: list of paths to concat (must all be same resolution/fps for stream-copy). re_encode: True = re-encode to ensure compatibility (recommended). Returns: {output_path, duration_s, clip_count}
tools.name: vid_concat

tools.description: Export video with platform-optimized encoding preset. platform: youtube_4k, youtube_1080, youtube_shorts, tiktok, instagram_reels, instagram_feed, twitter, facebook, linkedin, prores_4444, prores_422, h265_4k, av1_web, gif, web_mp4. Returns: {output_path, platform, size_mb}
tools.name: vid_export

tools.description: Export video as HLS adaptive bitrate ladder (for streaming). Creates 3 renditions: 1080p, 720p, 480p + master playlist. output_subdir: directory name inside OUTPUT_DIR for HLS files. Returns: {playlist_path, renditions}
tools.name: vid_export_hls

tools.description: Apply a raw FFmpeg -vf filter string to a video. filter_string: any valid FFmpeg video filter chain, e.g. 'eq=brightness=0.1:saturation=1.5' or 'gblur=sigma=5,vignette'. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_filter

tools.description: Apply retro/glitch effects. style: 'vhs' = VHS tape look, 'rgb_split' = color channel separation, 'scanlines' = CRT scanline overlay, 'datamosh' = pixel smear effect. intensity: 1–15 (effect strength). Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_glitch

tools.description: Apply a cinematic color grade preset. look: teal_orange, vintage_film, blockbuster, noir, warm_golden, cold_blue, lifted_blacks, flat. grain: 0=no grain, 5=subtle, 10=moderate, 18=heavy film grain. Returns: {output_path, look}
tools.name: vid_grade

tools.description: Add cinematic film grain. Luma-only (more authentic). strength: 5=subtle, 10=moderate, 18=heavy analog film. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_grain

tools.description: Add cinematic film halation — red/orange glow around bright highlights. strength: 0.2=subtle, 0.45=authentic film, 0.8=heavy. glow_radius: gaussian blur radius for glow spread (default 18). Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_halation

tools.description: Inspect a video file — returns duration, fps, resolution, codecs, size. path: absolute path inside workspace/input/output dirs.
tools.name: vid_inspect

tools.description: List video files available in the workspace/output directories. subdir: optional subdirectory name within OUTPUT_DIR to list. Returns dict with 'workspace', 'output', 'input' file lists.
tools.name: vid_list_workspace

tools.description: Loop a video clip N times or to fill a target duration. loop_count: number of times to repeat (-1 if using total_duration_s). total_duration_s: if > 0, loop until this duration is reached. Returns: {output_path, duration_s}
tools.name: vid_loop

tools.description: Add a professional animated lower third (name + job title) to a video. Accent bar slides in from left, then name and title fade up. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_lower_third

tools.description: Apply a .cube LUT file to a video. lut_path: path to .cube LUT file (must be in E:/NIRA_VIDEO_MCP/luts/ or workspace). intensity: 0.0–1.0 blend strength (1.0 = full LUT, 0.5 = 50% mix with original). chain_filters: optional additional -vf filters to append after LUT. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_lut

tools.description: Render a Manim Community animation from Python scene code. scene_code: complete Python source defining a Scene subclass. scene_class: name of the Scene class to render. quality: 'l'=480p, 'm'=720p, 'h'=1080p, 'k'=4K. Returns: {output_path, render_id} Runs as background job — poll render_status for completion.
tools.name: vid_manim_render

tools.description: Read or write video file metadata (title, artist, year, comment, etc.). read_only: True = just return current metadata, no output file. metadata: dict of key/value pairs to embed (e.g. {"title": "My Video", "year": "2026"}). Returns: {output_path} when writing, or {metadata} when reading.
tools.name: vid_metadata

tools.description: Add motion blur by blending adjacent frames (simulates 180° film shutter). frames: 2=subtle, 4=cinematic, 8=heavy blur (slow motion look). Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_motion_blur

tools.description: Composite one video over another (picture-in-picture / watermark). base_path: background video. overlay_path: video or image to composite on top. x, y: pixel offset for overlay (top-left corner). opacity: 0.0–1.0. start_s / end_s: time range when overlay is visible (-1 = full duration). Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_overlay

tools.description: Full ffprobe JSON dump for a video — all streams, format metadata. Use vid_inspect for a quick summary.
tools.name: vid_probe

tools.description: Add an animated progress bar that fills across the video duration. position: 'top' or 'bottom'. color: hex color or named color. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_progress_bar

tools.description: Resize video to target dimensions. fit: 'contain' = letterbox/pillarbox (no crop), 'cover' = crop to fill, 'stretch' = distort to exact size. Returns: {output_path, width, height}
tools.name: vid_resize

tools.description: Reverse a video clip (plays backwards). Audio is also reversed. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_reverse

tools.description: Change video playback speed. speed: 0.25 = 4x slow motion, 0.5 = 2x slow, 1.0 = normal, 2.0 = 2x fast, 4.0 = 4x fast. Audio is pitch-shifted accordingly. Returns: {output_path, duration_s, speed}
tools.name: vid_speed

tools.description: Stabilize shaky video footage (two-pass vidstab). smoothing: 10=moderate, 30=smooth, 100=locked-off tripod look. shakiness: 1–10, how shaky the source is. Returns: {output_path, render_id} — runs as background job (may take a while).
tools.name: vid_stabilize

tools.description: Add subtitles to a video from an SRT file. burn_in: True = render text into frames (compatible everywhere). False = add as soft subtitle track (MKV/MP4 container only). Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_subtitles

tools.description: Add animated text overlay to a video. position: 'center', 'top', 'bottom', 'top_left', 'top_right', 'bottom_left', 'bottom_right', or 'x=100:y=200'. animation: 'fade', 'slide_up', 'typewriter', 'none'. duration_s: -1 = entire video. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_text_overlay

tools.description: Extract a single frame from a video as a JPEG image. timestamp_seconds: position in video to grab (default 1.0s). width: output thumbnail width in pixels (height auto-scaled).
tools.name: vid_thumbnail

tools.description: Generate a thumbnail sprite sheet (contact sheet) for video scrubbing UIs. interval_s: how many seconds between each thumbnail. thumb_width: width of each thumbnail in pixels. Returns: {output_path, count, columns}
tools.name: vid_thumbnail_sprite

tools.description: Generate a standalone animated title card video (no input needed). Title slides up and fades in, then fades out. Use vid_concat to prepend it to another clip. Returns: {output_path, duration_s}
tools.name: vid_title_card

tools.description: Concatenate two clips with an xfade transition between them. transition: fade, dissolve, wipeleft, wiperight, wipeup, wipedown, slideleft, slideright, slideup, slidedown, circlecrop, rectcrop, distance, radial, smoothleft, smoothright, smoothup, smoothdown, circleopen, circleclose, vertopen, vertclose, horzopen, horzclose, fadegrays, pixelize. duration_s: length of the crossfade (default 1.0s). Returns: {output_path, duration_s}
tools.name: vid_transition

tools.description: Trim a video to a start/end time range. start_seconds: trim start (default 0). end_seconds: trim end (-1 = until end of file). re_encode: False = stream-copy (fast, may be slightly imprecise at cut points). True = re-encode (slow, frame-accurate). Returns: {output_path, duration_s}
tools.name: vid_trim

tools.description: Add a cinematic vignette (dark edges) to a video. strength: 0.2=subtle, 0.5=moderate, 0.8=heavy. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_vignette

tools.description: Generate an audio waveform image from a video file. Returns a PNG image showing the audio waveform.
tools.name: vid_waveform

Returns: {render_id, output_path, estimated_cost_usd} — background job.
tools.name: ai_gen_fal

tools.description: List all available AI video generation models with pricing and capabilities. Returns: {models: [...]}
tools.name: ai_gen_list_models

tools.description: Check the status of an AI video generation job. Returns: {render_id, state, progress, output_path, error}
tools.name: ai_gen_status

tools.description: Generate a video using local Wan2GP (FREE, runs on your 4090). prompt: describe the video you want to generate. duration_frames: number of frames (81=~3s, 121=~5s at 24fps). resolution: '832*480' (fast) or '1280*720' (HD) or '480*832' (vertical). steps: 8 = fast draft, 20 = quality. nsfw_mode: True = adds NSFW LoRA (wan_general_nsfw_v3 at 1.75). image_path: optional input image for image-to-video generation. Returns: {render_id, output_path} — background job.
tools.name: ai_gen_wan2gp

tools.description: Add background music to a video, mixing with existing audio. music_volume: 0.1=very quiet background, 0.25=subtle, 0.5=equal mix. duck_under_voice: reduce music when original audio is loud (sidechain ducking). fade_out_s: music fade-out duration at end. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: aud_add_music

tools.description: Detect BPM and beat timestamps for beat-synced video editing. Uses scipy STFT + autocorrelation (librosa-free, numpy 2.4 compatible). energy: 'low' (cut every 8 beats = slow/cinematic), 'medium' (every 4 beats = bar cuts), 'high' (every 2 beats = energetic). video_duration: if provided, filters cuts to within video length. Returns: {bpm, tempo_confidence, beat_times, cut_points, total_beats}
tools.name: aud_detect_beats

tools.description: Smart sidechain audio ducking: music automatically ducks under voice/dialogue. video_path: video (or audio) containing the voice/narration track. music_path: background music file to duck. duck_db: how many dB to reduce music when voice is active. -12 = moderate, -20 = heavy. attack_ms/release_ms: how fast ducking engages and releases. Returns: {output_path, duck_db}
tools.name: aud_duck_smart

tools.description: Extract audio track from a video file. format: 'wav', 'mp3', 'aac', 'flac'. Returns: {output_path, duration_s}
tools.name: aud_extract

tools.description: Full professional mastering chain: EQ → compression → limiting → EBU R128 loudnorm. style: 'music' (-14 LUFS, presence boost, punchy comp), 'podcast' (-16 LUFS, speech-optimised), 'broadcast' (-23 LUFS, EBU R128 strict). target_lufs: override loudness target (ignored if style is 'broadcast'). Works on audio files and video files (passes video stream through unchanged). Returns: {output_path, style, lufs_applied}
tools.name: aud_master

tools.description: Mix multiple audio/video files' audio tracks together. input_paths: up to 8 files to mix. volumes: per-track volume multipliers (1.0 = unity). Defaults to equal mix. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: aud_mix

tools.description: Normalize audio to a target loudness (EBU R128 two-pass). target_lufs: -16.0 = YouTube/streaming, -23.0 = broadcast/EBU R128, -14.0 = Spotify. Returns: {output_path, target_lufs}
tools.name: aud_normalize

tools.description: Replace the audio track of a video with a new audio file. mix_original: 0.0 = completely replace, 0.3 = 30% original + 70% new audio. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: aud_replace

tools.description: Remove audio from a video (mute / silent output). Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: aud_silence

tools.description: Create a named video project to track multiple clips and settings. name: project name (used as identifier). clips: optional list of initial clip paths to add. Returns: {project_id, name, clip_count}
tools.name: proj_create

tools.description: List all projects, or get details for a specific project. project_id: if empty, lists all projects. If set, returns that project's clips. Returns: {projects: [...]} or {project: {..., clips: [...]}}
tools.name: proj_list

tools.description: Render all clips in a project as a single final video. Clips are concatenated in order with optional transitions between them. transition: 'none', 'fade', 'dissolve', 'wipeleft', 'wiperight'. music_path: optional background music track to add. Returns: {render_id, output_path} — runs as background job.
tools.name: proj_render

tools.description: Cancel a running background render job. render_id: the render_id of the job to cancel. Returns: {render_id, state}
tools.name: render_cancel

tools.description: List all render jobs (running, completed, failed). Returns: {jobs: [...], counts: {running, done, failed, cancelled}}
tools.name: render_list

tools.description: Check the status of any background render job. render_id: the render_id returned when a background job was started. Returns: {render_id, state, progress, output_path, error, description} States: pending, running, done, failed, cancelled
tools.name: render_status

tools.description: Embed chapter markers into a video file. chapters: list of {title: str, start_s: float} dicts. Example: [{"title": "Intro", "start_s": 0}, {"title": "Demo", "start_s": 30}] Returns: {output_path, chapter_count}
tools.name: vid_chapters

tools.description: Remove green/blue screen and composite over a background. foreground_path: footage with green/blue screen. background_path: background video or image. key_color: 'green', 'blue', or hex like '0x3CB043'. similarity: 0.1 = tight key (needs clean lighting), 0.3 = loose key. blend: 0.0 = hard edge, 0.15 = soft anti-aliased edge. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_chromakey

tools.description: Concatenate multiple video clips in order. input_paths: list of paths to concat (must all be same resolution/fps for stream-copy). re_encode: True = re-encode to ensure compatibility (recommended). Returns: {output_path, duration_s, clip_count}
tools.name: vid_concat

tools.description: Export video with platform-optimized encoding preset. platform: youtube_4k, youtube_1080, youtube_shorts, tiktok, instagram_reels, instagram_feed, twitter, facebook, linkedin, prores_4444, prores_422, h265_4k, av1_web, gif, web_mp4. Returns: {output_path, platform, size_mb}
tools.name: vid_export

tools.description: Export video as HLS adaptive bitrate ladder (for streaming). Creates 3 renditions: 1080p, 720p, 480p + master playlist. output_subdir: directory name inside OUTPUT_DIR for HLS files. Returns: {playlist_path, renditions}
tools.name: vid_export_hls

tools.description: Apply a raw FFmpeg -vf filter string to a video. filter_string: any valid FFmpeg video filter chain, e.g. 'eq=brightness=0.1:saturation=1.5' or 'gblur=sigma=5,vignette'. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_filter

tools.description: Apply retro/glitch effects. style: 'vhs' = VHS tape look, 'rgb_split' = color channel separation, 'scanlines' = CRT scanline overlay, 'datamosh' = pixel smear effect. intensity: 1–15 (effect strength). Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_glitch

tools.description: Apply a cinematic color grade preset. look: teal_orange, vintage_film, blockbuster, noir, warm_golden, cold_blue, lifted_blacks, flat. grain: 0=no grain, 5=subtle, 10=moderate, 18=heavy film grain. Returns: {output_path, look}
tools.name: vid_grade

tools.description: Add cinematic film grain. Luma-only (more authentic). strength: 5=subtle, 10=moderate, 18=heavy analog film. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_grain

tools.description: Add cinematic film halation — red/orange glow around bright highlights. strength: 0.2=subtle, 0.45=authentic film, 0.8=heavy. glow_radius: gaussian blur radius for glow spread (default 18). Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_halation

tools.description: Inspect a video file — returns duration, fps, resolution, codecs, size. path: absolute path inside workspace/input/output dirs.
tools.name: vid_inspect

tools.description: List video files available in the workspace/output directories. subdir: optional subdirectory name within OUTPUT_DIR to list. Returns dict with 'workspace', 'output', 'input' file lists.
tools.name: vid_list_workspace

tools.description: Loop a video clip N times or to fill a target duration. loop_count: number of times to repeat (-1 if using total_duration_s). total_duration_s: if > 0, loop until this duration is reached. Returns: {output_path, duration_s}
tools.name: vid_loop

tools.description: Add a professional animated lower third (name + job title) to a video. Accent bar slides in from left, then name and title fade up. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_lower_third

tools.description: Apply a .cube LUT file to a video. lut_path: path to .cube LUT file (must be in E:/NIRA_VIDEO_MCP/luts/ or workspace). intensity: 0.0–1.0 blend strength (1.0 = full LUT, 0.5 = 50% mix with original). chain_filters: optional additional -vf filters to append after LUT. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_lut

tools.description: Render a Manim Community animation from Python scene code. scene_code: complete Python source defining a Scene subclass. scene_class: name of the Scene class to render. quality: 'l'=480p, 'm'=720p, 'h'=1080p, 'k'=4K. Returns: {output_path, render_id} Runs as background job — poll render_status for completion.
tools.name: vid_manim_render

tools.description: Read or write video file metadata (title, artist, year, comment, etc.). read_only: True = just return current metadata, no output file. metadata: dict of key/value pairs to embed (e.g. {"title": "My Video", "year": "2026"}). Returns: {output_path} when writing, or {metadata} when reading.
tools.name: vid_metadata

tools.description: Add motion blur by blending adjacent frames (simulates 180° film shutter). frames: 2=subtle, 4=cinematic, 8=heavy blur (slow motion look). Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_motion_blur

tools.description: Composite one video over another (picture-in-picture / watermark). base_path: background video. overlay_path: video or image to composite on top. x, y: pixel offset for overlay (top-left corner). opacity: 0.0–1.0. start_s / end_s: time range when overlay is visible (-1 = full duration). Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_overlay

tools.description: Full ffprobe JSON dump for a video — all streams, format metadata. Use vid_inspect for a quick summary.
tools.name: vid_probe

tools.description: Add an animated progress bar that fills across the video duration. position: 'top' or 'bottom'. color: hex color or named color. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_progress_bar

tools.description: Resize video to target dimensions. fit: 'contain' = letterbox/pillarbox (no crop), 'cover' = crop to fill, 'stretch' = distort to exact size. Returns: {output_path, width, height}
tools.name: vid_resize

tools.description: Reverse a video clip (plays backwards). Audio is also reversed. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_reverse

tools.description: Change video playback speed. speed: 0.25 = 4x slow motion, 0.5 = 2x slow, 1.0 = normal, 2.0 = 2x fast, 4.0 = 4x fast. Audio is pitch-shifted accordingly. Returns: {output_path, duration_s, speed}
tools.name: vid_speed

tools.description: Stabilize shaky video footage (two-pass vidstab). smoothing: 10=moderate, 30=smooth, 100=locked-off tripod look. shakiness: 1–10, how shaky the source is. Returns: {output_path, render_id} — runs as background job (may take a while).
tools.name: vid_stabilize

tools.description: Add subtitles to a video from an SRT file. burn_in: True = render text into frames (compatible everywhere). False = add as soft subtitle track (MKV/MP4 container only). Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_subtitles

tools.description: Add animated text overlay to a video. position: 'center', 'top', 'bottom', 'top_left', 'top_right', 'bottom_left', 'bottom_right', or 'x=100:y=200'. animation: 'fade', 'slide_up', 'typewriter', 'none'. duration_s: -1 = entire video. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_text_overlay

tools.description: Extract a single frame from a video as a JPEG image. timestamp_seconds: position in video to grab (default 1.0s). width: output thumbnail width in pixels (height auto-scaled).
tools.name: vid_thumbnail

tools.description: Generate a thumbnail sprite sheet (contact sheet) for video scrubbing UIs. interval_s: how many seconds between each thumbnail. thumb_width: width of each thumbnail in pixels. Returns: {output_path, count, columns}
tools.name: vid_thumbnail_sprite

tools.description: Generate a standalone animated title card video (no input needed). Title slides up and fades in, then fades out. Use vid_concat to prepend it to another clip. Returns: {output_path, duration_s}
tools.name: vid_title_card

tools.description: Concatenate two clips with an xfade transition between them. transition: fade, dissolve, wipeleft, wiperight, wipeup, wipedown, slideleft, slideright, slideup, slidedown, circlecrop, rectcrop, distance, radial, smoothleft, smoothright, smoothup, smoothdown, circleopen, circleclose, vertopen, vertclose, horzopen, horzclose, fadegrays, pixelize. duration_s: length of the crossfade (default 1.0s). tools.name: vid_transition

tools.description: Trim a video to a start/end time range. start_seconds: trim start (default 0). end_seconds: trim end (-1 = until end of file). re_encode: False = stream-copy (fast, may be slightly imprecise at cut points). True = re-encode (slow, frame-accurate). Returns: {output_path, duration_s}

tools.description: Generate TTS voiceover from script using ElevenLabs, mix with video, and optionally produce SRT caption file with word-level timestamps. tools.description: Add a cinematic vignette (dark edges) to a video. strength: 0.2=subtle, 0.5=moderate, 0.8=heavy. Returns: {output_path}

tools.description: Extract a single frame from a video as a JPEG image. timestamp_seconds: position in video to grab (default 1.0s). width: output thumbnail width in pixels (height auto-scaled).
tools.name: vid_thumbnail

tools.description: Generate a thumbnail sprite sheet (contact sheet) for video scrubbing UIs. interval_s: how many seconds between each thumbnail. thumb_width: width of each thumbnail in pixels. Returns: {output_path, count, columns}
tools.name: vid_thumbnail_sprite

tools.description: Generate a standalone animated title card video (no input needed). Title slides up and fades in, then fades out. Use vid_concat to prepend it to another clip. Returns: {output_path, duration_s}
tools.name: vid_title_card

tools.description: Concatenate two clips with an xfade transition between them. transition: fade, dissolve, wipeleft, wiperight, wipeup, wipedown, slideleft, slideright, slideup, slidedown, circlecrop, rectcrop, distance, radial, smoothleft, smoothright, smoothup, smoothdown, circleopen, circleclose, vertopen, vertclose, horzopen, horzclose, fadegrays, pixelize. duration_s: length of the crossfade (default 1.0s). Returns: {output_path, duration_s}
tools.name: vid_transition

tools.description: Trim a video to a start/end time range. start_seconds: trim start (default 0). end_seconds: trim end (-1 = until end of file). re_encode: False = stream-copy (fast, may be slightly imprecise at cut points). True = re-encode (slow, frame-accurate). Returns: {output_path, duration_s}
tools.name: vid_trim

tools.description: Generate TTS voiceover from script using ElevenLabs, mix with video, and optionally produce SRT caption file with word-level timestamps. Requires ELEVENLABS_API_KEY environment variable. voice_id: ElevenLabs voice ID. Default = Rachel (calm narration). Other voices: AZnzlk1XvdvUeBnXmlld (Domi), TxGEqnHWrfWFTfGW9XjX (Josh/deep). mix_volume: volume of TTS voice in final mix (1.0 = full, 0.7 = slightly under). background_music_path: optional music to mix under the voiceover (auto-ducked). music_volume: music level under voice (0.15-0.25 recommended). generate_srt: if True, also produce an SRT subtitle file alongside the video. Returns: {output_path, srt_path (if generated), voice_duration_s, voice_audio_path}
tools.name: vid_tts_caption

tools.description: Add a cinematic vignette (dark edges) to a video. strength: 0.2=subtle, 0.5=moderate, 0.8=heavy. Returns: {output_path}
tools.name: vid_vignette

tools.description: Generate an audio waveform image from a video file. Returns a PNG image showing the audio waveform.
tools.name: vid_waveform

tools.description: Analyze code for smells and suggest refactorings. Detects code smells like long methods, large classes, feature envy, and suggests appropriate refactorings to address them. Note: This feature requires backend support. Returns backend_supported: false for backends that don't implement analysis yet. Args: path: File or directory path to analyze smells: Optional list of smell types to check for (e.g., ['long-method', 'large-class', 'feature-envy']) Returns: TOON-formatted string with analysis results. Supported smell types (when backend supports analysis): - long-method: Method exceeds line threshold - large-class: Class has too many responsibilities - feature-envy: Method uses another class's data excessively - data-clumps: Same data items appear together repeatedly - primitive-obsession: Overuse of primitives instead of objects - duplicate-code: Similar code in multiple locations
tools.name: analyze_code

tools.description: Apply a refactoring to the codebase. This actually modifies files. Use preview_refactoring first to see what changes will be made. Changes can be reverted with git. Args: refactoring: Name of the refactoring (e.g., 'extract-method') target: Target in language-native format (e.g., 'src/order.py::Order::calculate#L10-L15') params: Refactoring-specific parameters Returns: TOON-formatted string with results of the applied refactoring. Example: apply_refactoring( refactoring="rename-method", target="src/order.py::Order::calc_total", params={"new_name": "calculate_total"} )
tools.name: apply_refactoring

tools.description: Get structural information about code (classes, methods, line numbers). Inspects a file to return information about its structure. Use this to understand the code before applying refactorings. Args: path: File path to inspect (e.g., 'src/order.py') depth: Level of detail - 'file', 'class', or 'method' (default: 'class') Returns: TOON-formatted string with structural information. Example: inspect_structure(path="src/order.py", depth="method")
tools.name: inspect_structure

tools.description: List available refactorings with their parameter contracts. Returns the catalog of available refactorings from all enabled backends, optionally filtered by language and/or category. Args: language: Filter by language (e.g., 'python'). If not specified, returns all. category: Filter by Fowler category (e.g., 'composing_methods') Returns: TOON-formatted string containing refactoring specifications. Categories: - composing_methods: Extract/inline methods, variables - moving_features: Move methods/fields between classes - organizing_data: Encapsulation, type codes - simplifying_conditionals: Guard clauses, polymorphism - simplifying_method_calls: Rename, add/remove parameters - dealing_with_generalization: Pull up/push down, inheritance
tools.name: list_refactorings

tools.description: Preview what changes a refactoring would make without applying them. This is a dry-run mode that shows the diff of what would change, without actually modifying any files. Always preview before applying. Args: refactoring: Name of the refactoring (e.g., 'extract-method') target: Target in language-native format (e.g., 'src/order.py::Order::calculate#L10-L15') params: Refactoring-specific parameters (e.g., {'name': 'calculate_tax'}) Returns: TOON-formatted string with preview results including diff. Example: preview_refactoring( refactoring="extract-method", target="src/order.py::Order::calculate#L10-L15", params={"name": "calculate_tax"} )
tools.name: preview_refactoring

tools.description: View documentation about a GitHub repository from Google CodeWiki. Without ``section_title``, returns the full wiki content (may be truncated). With ``section_title``, returns just that section's content. Use ``codewiki_read_structure`` first to see available sections. **Pagination** (when ``section_title`` is empty): - ``offset`` — section index to start from (default 0). - ``limit`` — max sections per response (default 5). The response includes ``has_more`` and ``next_offset`` when more sections are available, so you can call again to continue. **Response size**: 2–10 KB per section, 5–30 KB for paginated full page. Cached for 5 minutes — repeated calls are instant. **Rate limit**: max 10 calls per 60 s per repo URL. Duplicate concurrent calls are automatically deduplicated. Args: repo_url: Full repository URL (e.g. https://github.com/facebook/react) or shorthand owner/repo (e.g. facebook/react). Bare keywords (e.g. 'react') are auto-resolved with interactive disambiguation. section_title: Optional. Title (or partial title) of a specific section to retrieve. If empty, returns the full wiki. offset: Section index to start from (0-based, default 0). limit: Maximum sections to return (default 5, max 50).
tools.name: codewiki_read_contents

tools.description: Get a list of documentation topics for a repository from Google CodeWiki. Returns the table of contents / section structure as a JSON list so you can choose which sections to read with ``codewiki_read_contents``. **Recommended first step** — call this before ``codewiki_read_contents`` or ``codewiki_list_topics`` to discover available sections without consuming many tokens. **Response size**: typically 1–3 KB (lightweight JSON). Cached for 5 minutes — repeated calls are instant. **Rate limit**: max 10 calls per 60 s per repo URL. Duplicate concurrent calls are automatically deduplicated. Args: repo_url: Full repository URL (e.g. https://github.com/facebook/react) or shorthand owner/repo (e.g. facebook/react). Bare keywords (e.g. 'react') are auto-resolved with interactive disambiguation.
tools.name: codewiki_read_structure

tools.description: Request Google CodeWiki to index a repository that is not yet available. Use this tool when ``codewiki_list_topics`` or ``codewiki_read_structure`` returns a ``NOT_INDEXED`` error, indicating the repository has no CodeWiki documentation yet. This tool will: 1. Search for the repository on CodeWiki. 2. Click "Request repository" to open the submission dialog. 3. Fill in the GitHub URL and submit the request. 4. Return confirmation and next-step guidance. **Note**: Google CodeWiki reviews requests and indexes repositories based on popularity and demand. There is no guaranteed timeline. Args: repo_url: Full repository URL (e.g. https://github.com/owner/repo) or shorthand owner/repo (e.g. owner/repo). Bare keywords (e.g. 'vue') are auto-resolved with interactive disambiguation.
tools.name: codewiki_request_indexing

tools.description: Ask Google CodeWiki a question about an open-source repository. This uses the interactive chat feature powered by Gemini. For reading wiki content directly, use ``codewiki_read_contents`` instead. Results are cached for 2 minutes — repeated identical queries are instant. **Response size**: typically 0.5–5 KB depending on the answer. **Rate limit**: max 10 calls per 60 s per repo URL. Args: repo_url: Full repository URL (e.g. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat) or shorthand owner/repo (e.g. microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat). Bare keywords (e.g. 'vue') are auto-resolved with interactive disambiguation. query: The question to ask (required).
tools.name: codewiki_search_wiki

tools.description: Retrieve metadata from a PDF without reading its full text. Returns title, author, subject, keywords, creator, producer, creation date, and page count. Args: source: Local file path or URL to the PDF. Returns: Formatted metadata string.
tools.name: get_metadata

tools.description: Extract text from a specific page range of a PDF. Pages are 1-indexed. If end_page is not specified, only start_page is read. Args: source: Local file path or URL to the PDF. start_page: First page to read (1-indexed). Defaults to 1. end_page: Last page to read (1-indexed, inclusive). Defaults to start_page if not specified. max_bytes: Maximum output size in bytes. Defaults to 200000. Returns: Extracted text from the specified pages.
tools.name: get_page

tools.description: Extract text from a PDF file or URL. Reads up to max_pages pages and max_bytes bytes of content. Scanned or image-based PDFs will be flagged as unreadable. Args: source: Local file path or URL to the PDF. max_pages: Maximum number of pages to read. Defaults to 50. max_bytes: Maximum output size in bytes. Defaults to 200000. Returns: Extracted text with page markers, or an error message.
tools.name: read_pdf
